item.title: FDIC publishes GENIUS Act PPSI reporting forms for PRA comment (FR Doc. 2026-14589, 91 FR 45274)
item.category: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
item.description:
On July 20, 2026 (filed on public inspection July 17), the FDIC published a Paperwork Reduction Act notice (FR Doc. 2026-14589, 91 FR 45274) requesting 60-day public comment on proposed weekly and quarterly reporting forms for FDIC-supervised Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers (PPSIs). The notice is associated with the FDIC's GENIUS Act PPSI NPRM (April 10, 2026, 91 FR 18534). Weekly Form PS-01 (for PPSIs with $1 billion or more in total outstanding issuance value or $100 million or more in average daily transaction volume) includes eight schedules covering top holders, top exchanges, trading volume, top counterparties, capital, issuance and redemption, and reserve assets disaggregated by type (cash and deposits, U.S. Treasuries by CUSIP, reverse repurchase agreements, money market mutual funds, and other instruments). Weekly Form PS-01a (smaller PPSIs) has three schedules. Quarterly Form PS-02 covers income statement, balance sheet, off-balance sheet items, capital and operational backstop, and memoranda including blockchain activity, redemption metrics, and custody activities. The FDIC estimates approximately 30 FDIC-supervised institutions would perform PPSI activities; ongoing weekly reporting burden estimated at 2,080 hours per year and quarterly at 800 hours. The publication confirms the FDIC GENIUS Act implementing final rule was not published as of the July 18, 2026 statutory one-year deadline. Comment period closes September 18, 2026.
Primary source: Federal Register — FDIC Notice, FR Doc. 2026-14589 (91 FR 45274), July 20, 2026 — https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/20/2026-14589/reporting-forms-and-instructions-associated-with-requirements-and-standards-for-fdic-supervised

item.title: Fed Chair Warsh testifies to House Financial Services: no Federal Reserve bailout for crypto or stablecoins; Fed 'racing' to meet GENIUS Act stablecoin rulemaking deadline; nonbank fintech payment access pressed
item.category: Federal Reserve Board
item.description:
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh testified before the House Committee on Financial Services on July 14, 2026, as part of the Semiannual Monetary Policy Report (2128 Rayburn House Office Building, 10:00 AM). The official prepared statement focused on price stability, monetary policy, and internal Fed task forces. During the Q&A, Warsh made three statements directly relevant to crypto, stablecoin, and fintech operators: (1) No Federal Reserve bailout for crypto or stablecoins: Pressed by Rep. Brad Sherman on whether the Fed would provide the kind of support it gave money market funds in 2008, Warsh stated 'We do not want to be in the bailout business, full stop.' He added that the Fed would 'do everything we can to mitigate... extraordinary risks' but would not bail out crypto. He did not fully rule out marginal systemic-spillover mitigation. (2) GENIUS Act rulemaking urgency: Warsh told lawmakers the Fed is 'racing' to finalize its portion of the GENIUS Act stablecoin implementing rules ahead of the July 18, 2026 one-year statutory deadline. The deadline has since been confirmed missed (the Federal Register contains no in-scope publication; July 18 is a Saturday; earliest possible publication is Monday July 20). (3) Nonbank fintech payment-system access: Rep. Sherman separately pressed on Kraken's pending bank application and nonbank crypto firms seeking direct access to the payment system; Warsh invoked systemic-risk considerations without making a specific commitment. Background: Warsh is the most crypto-sympathetic Fed Chair on record, having previously disclosed venture stakes in Bitcoin payments, a crypto index manager, Bitwise, and a stablecoin venture â all divested under Fed ethics rules prior to confirmation in May 2026. A 2026 New York Fed staff report cited in contemporaneous coverage found stablecoin activity can transmit liquidity stress to banks and complicate monetary policy. This is Warsh's first congressional testimony since his confirmation. Secondary coverage: Law360, July 14, 2026 ('Fed Racing To Hit Genius Act Rules Deadline, Warsh Says'); CCN via Yahoo Finance, July 15, 2026 ('Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Says Crypto and Stablecoins Are On Their Own in a Crisis').

item.title: CFTC stays KalshiEX rule change and uses emergency authority to order fulfillment of Michigan trades a state court directed be canceled (Release 9267-26)
item.category: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)
item.description:
On July 14, 2026, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced (Release 9267-26) that it exercised its authority to stay an emergency rule change proposed by KalshiEX, LLC in response to a Michigan state court order directing the company to cancel certain previously executed trades involving Michigan residents, and separately exercised its emergency authority to order KalshiEX to fulfill the open trades in accordance with its normal practices. Chairman Michael S. Selig stated that 'a state cannot force a DCM to violate its obligations, and federal law does not permit a DCM to discriminate against a state's residents,' and called canceling already-executed trades an 'unprecedented step' that risks a cascading effect on the marketplace. The Commission noted that Michigan is the first state to attempt to interfere directly with executed derivatives transactions and that it has filed lawsuits against Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, Kentucky, Minnesota, New Mexico, New York, Rhode Island, and Wisconsin to protect its jurisdiction.
Primary source: CFTC Press Release 9267-26 (July 14, 2026; primary source retrieved) — https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9267-26

item.title: Kalshi Seeks Emergency Injunction Pending Appeal in SDNY Case; New York Agrees to No-Enforcement Standstill Through July 30, Kalshi to Seek Second Circuit Relief July 23
item.category: KalshiEX LLC / U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York (No. 25-cv-08846-AT, Judge Analisa Torres)
item.description:
On July 15, 2026, KalshiEX LLC filed a letter motion in KalshiEX LLC v. Williams (No. 25-cv-08846-AT, S.D.N.Y., Judge Analisa Torres) seeking an emergency injunction pending appeal of the court's prior denial of a preliminary injunction. The filing states that defendants (New York state officials) agreed not to bring an enforcement action against Kalshi under New York law through July 30, 2026, while the motion is pending. If the court does not grant relief, Kalshi intends to seek a Second Circuit injunction pending appeal on July 23, 2026. The motion argues that the case presents serious legal questions about whether the Commodity Exchange Act preempts state gambling laws, noting the Third Circuit ruled for Kalshi in KalshiEX LLC v. Flaherty (172 F.4th 220, 3d Cir. 2026), while a separate federal preemption suit (CFTC v. New York, No. 26-cv-3404, S.D.N.Y., Judge Marrero) is pending in the same district. item.title: GENIUS Act stablecoin rulemaking deadline (July 18, 2026) one week out — six agencies had not finalized implementing rules as of July 11
item.category: OCC / FDIC / NCUA / U.S. Treasury / FinCEN / OFAC
item.description:
As of July 11, 2026, six federal agencies — the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA), the U.S. Treasury Department, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), and the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) — faced a statutory July 18, 2026 deadline (one year after the GENIUS Act's July 18, 2025 enactment) to finalize implementing rules for permitted payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs), and had not yet issued final rules. Comment periods on the proposed rules closed by early June 2026. The proposed framework requires PPSIs to hold 1:1 reserves in cash, insured deposits, and short-term U.S. Treasuries, and treats issuers as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act. Source: Tech Times (July 11, 2026); corroborated by CryptoSlate and rulemaking trackers (Chapman & Cutler, Paradigm).

item.title: First U.S. statutory ban on a Federal Reserve CBDC takes effect via the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R.6644 §1101)
item.category: U.S. Congress (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, H.R.6644 §1101)
item.description:
On July 10, 2026, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R.6644) became law without President Trump's signature. Per coverage by The Cryptonomist (July 10, 2026), corroborated by Tech Times (July 11, 2026) and CoinDesk (July 9-10, 2026), Section 1101 prohibits the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency (CBDC) or any substantially similar digital asset, directly or through an intermediary, through December 31, 2030. The bill passed the Senate 85-5 (June 22, 2026) and the House 358-32. Coverage reports a carve-out for open, permissionless, privately issued dollar-denominated digital assets (understood by coverage to include stablecoins). item.title: U.S.-UK Transatlantic Taskforce publishes recommendations on capital markets and digital assets, plus a joint statement on stablecoins
item.category: U.S. Department of the Treasury / HM Treasury
item.description:
On July 14, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury and HM Treasury jointly published recommendations of the Transatlantic Taskforce for Markets of the Future (Treasury press release SB0560). Treasury states the recommendations aim to deepen cross-border financial activity between the United States and the United Kingdom, reduce unnecessary frictions, and advance open, market-based standards, and that they identify opportunities to enhance cross-border capital raising, update supervisory cooperation, and provide clarity for tokenized financial activity. Following one of the Taskforce's recommendations, the United States and the UK released a joint statement on stablecoins the same day, which Treasury says supports dynamic cross-border stablecoin activity and highlights the key role of the private sector in the provision of money and payments. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Taskforce 'reflects the strength and depth of U.S. and UK markets and our shared commitment to fostering economic growth and advancing global standards that reward innovation and competition.' The Taskforce was established by Secretary Bessent and UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves in September 2025 and is co-chaired by U.S. Treasury and HM Treasury with participants from U.S. and UK financial sector regulatory agencies.

item.title: Michigan judge extends Kalshi sports-contract restraining order and sets Aug. 12 geofencing deadline with $500,000-per-day fines
item.category: Ingham County Circuit Court (Michigan) — Judge Rosemarie Aquilina
item.description:
As reported by Legal Sports Report and Gaming America on July 14, 2026, Ingham County Circuit Court Judge Rosemarie Aquilina heard arguments from the State of Michigan and KalshiEX on Monday, July 13, 2026, and extended the temporary restraining order against Kalshi's sports event contracts without setting an expiration date, ordering Kalshi to geofence the state by the end of day August 12, 2026. Per that coverage, if Kalshi does not geofence by that date it could face a $500,000 daily fine for violating the order, and Aquilina said Kalshi could also be punished under the initial $120,000-per-day penalties if it delays within the 30-day period, stating 'If you sit on it for 29 days, there will be sanctions.' Kalshi argued it falls under CFTC and Commodity Exchange Act regulation; Aquilina found conflict preemption did not apply because Kalshi can comply with both state and federal law simultaneously. The parties are scheduled to appear in court again the following week. The written order was not published on a free public docket and was not retrieved.

item.title: ICBA, ABA and 76 state banking associations urge Senate leaders to tighten CLARITY Act Section 404 stablecoin yield provisions
item.category: Independent Community Bankers of America / American Bankers Association
item.description:
As announced by the Independent Community Bankers of America on July 13, 2026, the American Bankers Association and ICBA, joined by 76 state associations, sent a letter to Senate Majority Leader John Thune and Minority Leader Charles Schumer urging targeted changes to the CLARITY Act to provide greater certainty that payment stablecoins cannot function as substitutes for bank deposits. The associations wrote that 'significant questions remain regarding whether the current language in Section 404 provides sufficient clarity and certainty to achieve that objective' and that 'ambiguities within the bill could encourage stablecoin arrangements to effectively function as substitutes for deposits, despite Congress's longstanding and clearly stated intent that payment stablecoins should serve as transaction tools rather than store-of-value products.' They urge revisions clarifying the prohibition on interest and yield, replacing the bill's 'functional and economic equivalent' standard with a 'substantially similar' standard, and removing language they believe could create ambiguity regarding rewards tied to stablecoin balances, duration or tenure. The underlying letter is linked from the announcement and was not independently retrieved.

item.title: SCOTUS rules 6-3 that for-cause removal protections for SEC and CFTC commissioners are unconstitutional (Trump v. Slaughter, No. 25-332)
item.category: U.S. Supreme Court
item.description:
On June 29, 2026, the Supreme Court of the United States issued its 6-3 opinion in Trump v. Slaughter (No. 25-332), authored by Chief Justice Roberts, overturning Humphrey's Executor v. United States (1935). The Court held that the for-cause removal protection in the FTC's enabling statute — and by structural extension the SEC and CFTC, which operate under identical removal provisions — is contrary to the separation of powers under the Constitution. Effective immediately, the President may remove SEC and CFTC commissioners without cause. A companion order in Trump v. Cook (No. 25A312, June 29, 2026) denied a government application to stay a preliminary injunction protecting Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook; the Federal Reserve's statutory structure was not directly addressed by the majority opinion. The opinion is published on the Court's official slip opinion list for October Term 2025.
